title: Dynamics 365 Contact Center: bullseye routing with user groups expands the eligible pool as wait time grows
summary: The briefing's roadmap facts, routing rules, prerequisites and publishing-credit trigger are supported by Microsoft's documentation. The documented delete endpoint is valid despite the automatic pre-check; minor corrections concern the creation path stopping before publication and a diagnostics checklist step without a controls-table entry.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Assignment starts with a targeted Level 0 user group and expands to additional user groups as wait time increases.
claims.quote: Bullseye routing starts assignment with a targeted Level 0 user group, then progressively expands the pool of eligible representatives to more user groups as wait time increases.

claims.claim: Earlier user groups remain active as the assignment pool expands.
claims.quote: User groups from earlier levels remain active and continue to be considered for assignment.

claims.claim: Representatives from earlier levels have priority over those added at later levels.
claims.quote: Representatives from previous levels receive higher priority than representatives added at later levels.

claims.claim: Bullseye expansion keeps the conversation in the same queue.
claims.quote: The conversation stays in the same queue throughout this process.

claims.claim: Administrators configure levels and wait times in a bullseye playbook for one or more queues.
claims.quote: Configure the playbook for one or more queues, with levels and wait times for routing.

claims.claim: Learn's example uses Expert support at Level 0, Regional support at 30 seconds and General support at 60 seconds.
claims.quote: Consider a configuration with three levels: Level 0 (Expert support group), Level 1 at 30 seconds (Regional support group), and Level 2 at 60 seconds (General support group).

claims.claim: The roadmap description supplies a similar three-tier example.
claims.quote:
0–30 seconds: Assign to Tier 1 specialists (primary user group)
- 30–60 seconds: Expand to include Tier 2 representatives (secondary user group)
- 60+ seconds: Include all available representatives (tertiary user group)

claims.claim: Wait time is cumulative from the first attempt to assign the conversation to a human representative.
claims.quote: Measures wait time cumulatively from when the system first attempts to assign the conversation to a human support representative.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The general minimum wait time is 30 seconds, subject to the stated Level 1 exception.
claims.quote: Sets the minimum wait time to at least 30 seconds.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Level 1 also supports a zero-second wait time.
claims.quote: Note that Level 1 also supports a 0 second wait time.

claims.claim: A later level may use the same wait time as the preceding level.
claims.quote: The next level wait time can be the same as the previous level or should increment by at least 10 seconds.

claims.claim: An increased wait time for a later level must increment by at least 10 seconds.
claims.quote: The next level wait time can be the same as the previous level or should increment by at least 10 seconds.

claims.claim: Transferring a conversation to another queue resets its wait time.
claims.quote: Resets the wait time and restarts evaluation from Level 0 in the new queue if a conversation is transferred to another queue.

claims.claim: After transfer to another queue, evaluation restarts at Level 0 in that queue.
claims.quote: Resets the wait time and restarts evaluation from Level 0 in the new queue if a conversation is transferred to another queue.
